fixes.explanation: Joseph wraps the body in linen and places it in a tomb cut into the rock. Luke tells us exactly where, so there's no guessing. The women from Galilee saw the tomb and how His body was placed (Luke 23:55). I think Joseph handled it with great care.
Luke says the tomb was one “…where no one had yet been laid.” (Luke 23:53) Nobody else had been placed in it before. Jesus is the first. I think that's worth noticing, friend.
Luke says the women who had come with Jesus from Galilee followed. They saw the tomb and how His body was placed. They were there, and they saw it. I think they wanted to know where He was.

The women find the stone rolled away from the tomb. They came with spices for a body, and what they find is an open tomb. I think that stopped them in their tracks. And Luke tells us it's only the beginning.

Joseph is the one who laid Jesus in the tomb, but Luke doesn't put him there that morning. What the women find is the stone rolled away from the tomb (Luke 24:2). Luke doesn't mention Joseph in that scene. The women have their spices, and the tomb is open.

That's not what Luke tells us. He says the women “…bowed their faces to the ground in terror…” (Luke 24:5) Two men in radiant apparel were suddenly beside them. Luke doesn't say they reached out to touch anyone. He says they bowed down with their faces to the ground.

Joseph is the one who placed Jesus in the tomb, but the two men don't say he moved Him. They say, “He is not here; He has risen!” (Luke 24:6) That's the news they give the women. Joseph doesn't come into it.

The women report all these things to the Eleven and to all the others. Luke says the ones who told it were Mary Magdalene, Joanna, Mary the mother of James and the other women with them. They told the apostles (Luke 24:10). I think they were eager to tell it.

You'd hope so, since the women saw it themselves. But Luke says, “But their words seemed like nonsense to them, and they did not believe the women.” (Luke 24:11) The apostles heard the report, and they didn't believe it. I bet that stung the women.

That's right, friend. Luke says, “But their words seemed like nonsense to them, and they did not believe the women.” (Luke 24:11) The women reported it, and to the apostles it seemed like nonsense. I think that was hard on the women.

Luke says Peter “…got up and ran to the tomb.” (Luke 24:12) Peter is one of the apostles, and the women's words had seemed like nonsense to them (Luke 24:11). But he doesn't sit still. He gets up and runs.

Joseph is the Council member who laid Jesus in the tomb, but Luke has Peter go somewhere else. Peter, one of the apostles, “…got up and ran to the tomb.” (Luke 24:12) Luke sends him straight to the tomb. That's where he goes.
